{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOLEgSIs8AAAABXFvy0Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm7fazhApie0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm7fa", "number": 3, "title": "Migrate all first-party JavaScript to TypeScript in a single PR", "body": "## Problem

The extension's maintained application and emulation code is written in JavaScript without TypeScript configuration or project-wide type checking. This makes cross-component contracts (extension messages, device configuration, and WebXR emulation) difficult to validate statically.

**The requested migration must be completed all at once in one cohesive PR, not as a staged or partial conversion across multiple PRs.**

## Expected outcome

Convert **all first-party, human-maintained JavaScript** in the repository to TypeScript in **a single PR targeting `dev`**. The build must emit the JavaScript artifacts that browsers require, and previously supported extension behavior must remain intact. No first-party source-migration work should be deferred to a later PR.

A Three.js update is **allowed if needed** to complete the migration or preserve compatibility. If necessary, move to a suitable current Three.js version and update affected loaders, controls, and APIs within the same PR; otherwise keep the current dependency to avoid unrelated changes.

## Context

- Follow [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/development-flow.md) and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/review-guidelines.md). Use English for the Issue, PR and commits; base work on `dev`.
- Maintained JavaScript exists in `src/polyfill/`, `src/extension/`, `src/app/panel.js`, and `src/ConfigurationManager.js`. Inspect for any other maintained JavaScript (including build configuration) and handle it in the same PR.
- `npm run build` currently bundles `src/polyfill/CustomWebXRPolyfill.js` with Rollup into `polyfill/webxr-polyfill.js`. The extension manifests/HTML load JS files directly. Maintain the injected polyfill's UMD/global `WebXRPolyfillInjection` contract, script order, startup timing, and runtime communication.
- `src/app/three/` contains vendored third-party JavaScript and `polyfill/webxr-polyfill.js` is a generated artifact; these do not need to become TypeScript source. External `webxr-polyfill` is also out of scope. Use appropriate types/shims rather than rewriting third-party code. If upgrading Three.js is necessary, update those vendor dependencies consistently.
- Fixing unrelated WebXR specification gaps or migrating to Manifest V3 is a separate issue, except for any changes truly required to preserve the TS migration's functionality.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Complete **all** maintained first-party JavaScript-to-TypeScript migration in **one PR**, with no phased or partial follow-up PRs for remaining source files.
- [ ] Convert maintained files across `src/polyfill/`, `src/extension/`, `src/app/` (excluding unmodified vendored `three/` assets) and `src/ConfigurationManager.js` to `.ts`/`.tsx` as appropriate; find and migrate any other first-party JS, or explicitly justify unavoidable exceptions.
- [ ] Add TypeScript tooling/configuration and a working `npm run typecheck` script. Introduce useful typings for XR/device/session state, controller poses, device definitions, cross-context extension messages/events, and browser APIs.
- [ ] Type-check **all** converted sources with meaningful checks; do not hide migration errors with blanket `any`, `@ts-nocheck`, or exclusions. Document any narrowly scoped third-party declarations or exceptions.
- [ ] Update `npm run build` to compile/bundle all TypeScript entry points into expected browser-compatible JavaScript files. Update `manifest.json`, HTML references and generated output as required. Preserve polyfill injection/global behavior, browser-context boundaries, and synchronous startup.
- [ ] Keep current VR, AR, DevTools UI, configuration persistence, controller input, and extension message passing behavior unchanged as far as the existing implementation supports.
- [ ] If a Three.js update is needed, justify it, use a compatible current release, migrate affected Three.js APIs and loaders/controls in **this same PR**, and validate the resulting 3D UI. Otherwise retain the existing version.
- [ ] Run `npm install`, `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck` and applicable tests/checks; inspect generated bundle changes, report real results, and resolve migration-caused failures.
- [ ] Validate the extension in a desktop browser/version that can load it: DevTools panel and device selection; persisted configuration; immersive VR with headset/controller movement and select/squeeze; existing immersive AR / hit-test behavior. Document tested browser and steps, and report pre-existing failures or Manifest V2 constraints separately rather than claiming success.
- [ ] Update README development/build instructions and affected source-path references without losing the useful existing install/build instructions.
- [ ] Open the single implementation PR against `dev` using the repository PR template and request review per the guidelines.

## Optional validation

- Smoke-test Firefox and a Chrome/Chromium setup that supports the current manifest, where available.
- Compare generated bundle behavior or representative WebXR sample applications before and after conversion.

## Required post-merge verification

None. All applicable build, type-check and browser checks are pre-merge validation.
